acceptance_test_matrix: 5-node graph.yaml fixture covers nodes, edges, partitions, and watermarks and loads through GraphYamlLoader.fromFile(Path).
Loaded CompiledPlan canonical bytes are exactly equal to a hand-built CompiledPlan for the same 5-node topology.
Unknown node type validation fails before compilation with an actionable error naming the unregistered type and related node context.
Invalid topology fixtures reject missing nodes, duplicate node ids, edges referencing absent nodes, invalid partitions, and invalid watermarks before runtime startup.
Deterministic ordering prevents byte drift across repeated loads.
Load-time measurement for the 5-node YAML fixture is below 100ms with YAML parsing confined to startup.
Configured QA gates pass: ./qa/smoke.sh, ./qa/regression.sh, and ./gradlew --no-daemon --console=plain test.
assumptions: GraphYamlLoader.fromFile(Path) is the required public startup entry point and may delegate to existing catalog and compiler APIs internally.
The loader belongs with graph definition and compilation contracts rather than runtime hot-path execution.
YAML references stable registered node type identifiers rather than arbitrary Java implementation class names.
Existing node catalog registration is the authority for valid node types.
Byte equivalence can be asserted using the repository's existing serialized or canonical CompiledPlan representation, or a deterministic helper under QA/test paths.
The 100ms load-time criterion applies to the required 5-node YAML fixture and measures startup parse plus compile work, not runtime execution.
No YAML schema versioning, hot reload, mutable runtime graph update, snapshot, journal, CRC, or recovery behavior is in scope for this feature.

critic.rationale: The plan satisfies most lifecycle, sequencing, verification, and governance checks. The main concerns are path coverage and QA/source disjointness: implementer slices allow build files that are not listed as affected surfaces, tests do not include a compiler-core test root despite compiler-core being the primary implementation surface, and the reviewer slice includes both source and test paths though reviewer writes are expected to be report-oriented. No final verdict is decided here.

acceptance_tests: A 5-node graph.yaml fixture loads through GraphYamlLoader.fromFile(Path).
The fixture covers nodes, edges, partitions, and watermarks.
Loaded CompiledPlan bytes exactly match a hand-built equivalent plan for the same 5-node topology.
Unknown node type fixture fails before compilation with an actionable error naming the unregistered type and related node context.
Malformed topology fixtures fail before runtime execution for missing nodes, duplicate node ids, edges referencing absent nodes, invalid partitions, and invalid watermarks.
Repeated loads of the same YAML fixture produce identical CompiledPlan bytes.
Load time for the 5-node fixture remains below 100ms.
./qa/smoke.sh, ./qa/regression.sh, and the Gradle test suite pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: The loader runs synchronously during startup before graph execution starts, constructs immutable graph definition data, publishes only the compiled plan, and introduces no file watcher, reload lock, live mutation path, or concurrent topology swap.
forbidden_alternatives: Do not add filesystem watchers or reloadable graph mutation APIs.
Do not bypass the registered node catalog with reflective class loading from YAML.
Do not encode Java implementation class names as the primary public schema contract.
Do not parse YAML inside runtime-core graph execution hot paths.
Do not add schema version negotiation or migrations.
Do not alter journal, snapshot, replay, CRC, recovery, or readiness semantics for this loader.
hard_constraints: Implement GraphYamlLoader.fromFile(Path).
Define YAML fields for nodes, edges, partitions, and watermarks.
Validate every node type against the registered node catalog before plan construction.
Unknown node type errors must identify the offending type and graph location or node id where available.
Reject malformed topology before runtime execution, including missing nodes, duplicate node ids, edges referencing absent nodes, invalid partitions, and invalid watermarks.
Canonicalize ordering for nodes, edges, partitions, and watermarks so repeated loads produce identical CompiledPlan bytes.
No YAML parsing is allowed on runtime execution hot paths.
No hot reload, file watching, or graph mutation from YAML edits is allowed.
No YAML schema versioning is introduced in this slice.
A 5-node YAML graph load test must complete below 100ms.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: compiler-core owns YAML schema mapping, validation, deterministic ordering, and CompiledPlan construction; dag-framework-api owns public API types if exposure is required; runtime-core remains a consumer of immutable compiled plans and must not parse YAML or depend on YAML loader internals.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: graph.yaml is an input configuration artifact read from Path during startup; the loader does not persist derived state, maintain schema migration metadata, create caches, or write journals, snapshots, CRCs, or runtime recovery data.
design_contract.public_api: Add GraphYamlLoader.fromFile(Path) as the startup entry point that reads graph.yaml, validates nodes, edges, partitions, and watermarks against the registered node catalog and graph constraints, and returns a deterministic CompiledPlan byte-equivalent to the hand-built plan.

final.problem_statement: Implement a startup-only YAML graph topology loader so graph.yaml can define nodes, edges, partitions, and watermarks without recompiling, while producing a deterministic CompiledPlan byte-equivalent to the current hand-built plan and keeping YAML parsing out of runtime hot paths.
risk_register: YAML schema may accidentally expose implementation class names instead of stable node type IDs.
YAML parser dependency or packaging changes may leak into runtime hot paths.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Loader runs synchronously during startup before graph execution; returned CompiledPlan is immutable/shareable; no hot reload, file watching, YAML edit mutation, or runtime graph mutation is allowed.
forbidden_alternatives: Do not parse YAML inside runtime-core graph execution hot paths.
Do not implement hot reload, file watching, or mutation through YAML edits.
Do not add YAML schema versioning for R-003.
Do not accept arbitrary class names from YAML as node implementations.
Do not add snapshot, CRC, journal, or recovery protocols unrelated to this startup loader.
hard_constraints: GraphYamlLoader.fromFile(Path) must be available and deterministic.
Schema must cover nodes, edges, partitions, and watermarks.
Unknown node types must fail before plan construction with actionable errors naming the missing type and YAML location or node id where available.
Loaded 5-node graph must be byte-equivalent to the hand-built CompiledPlan.
5-node fixture load time must be below 100ms.
YAML parsing must be startup-only and must not add allocations to runtime hot paths.
qa/smoke.sh must pass.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: compiler-core owns YAML schema mapping, validation, deterministic ordering, and CompiledPlan construction; dag-framework-api owns only public API types if exposure is required; runtime-core must consume only the returned immutable CompiledPlan and must not parse YAML.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: YAML is an input configuration file only; the loader must not create journals, snapshots, caches, schema migrations, or persistent runtime state in this slice.
design_contract.public_api: Add GraphYamlLoader.fromFile(Path) as the startup entry point that reads graph.yaml, validates nodes/edges/partitions/watermarks against the registered node catalog, and returns a deterministic CompiledPlan byte-equivalent to the hand-built plan.

Scope creep into schema versioning, hot reload, or persistence would violate R-003 constraints.
